messages:
maria: Heads-up — we need a short maintenance window on us-east1-rack-12 tomorrow 02:00-02:30 UTC. Vendor's swapping a fiber pair that services the rack. We'll do staggered node drains and rolling reboots. Aiming for no customer-facing downtime, but expect transient higher latency and partial GPU pool capacity reduction.

kevin: ETA on GPU capacity loss? we have a few large jobs scheduled overnight.

maria: Rough calc: ~20% capacity offline for ~10–15m at any one time while each host is rebooted and NIC re-attaches. We'll shift lower-priority batch jobs.

sasha: Recommend we run a canary first (2 nodes) and validate KV-cache warmup + prefix cache hit rates. If canary passes, continue. If not, abort and failover to eu-north1 burst capacity.

maria: Agreed. Plan: canary -> cohort of 6 nodes -> remaining nodes. Rollout order pinned to occupancy and thermal health.

ops-bot: Incident scheduled: maintenance/6732109876 — vendor fiber swap — 02:00 UTC. Auto-notify: #support and customers with impacted reserved pools.

kevin: What about Dedicated tenants pinned to these nodes? They need notices + SLA callouts.

lia: I'll draft the tenant notice. TL;DR: short rolling reboots, up to 15 mins impact per host, auto-fallback to backed-up pool for critical Reserved customers. Asking Product for approval now.

dan: One ask: include model-fallback policy for high-throughput endpoints. If quantized variants exist, route latency-sensitive traffic to the lighter model to keep P95 stable.

maria: Good point. We'll add a routing policy: during window route requests with latency tag >= 50ms to quantized-24q and reduce batch size for streaming sessions.

sasha: The drain command and verification checklist below — please copy into runbook before starting:
```
# drain and cordon
kubectl cordon node/$NODE
kubectl drain node/$NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m
# verify inference pods rescheduled and healthy
kubectl get pods -l app=inference -o wide | grep $NODE
# warm kv/cache seed
curl -s "http://cache-seed.local/seed?pool=us-east1-rack-12"
```

maria: We'll run telemetry checks: client-latency p95, token-cost spike, and active-inflight sessions. If token-cost > +15% or client-latency p95 > SLA threshold, pause.

kevin: Are we billing for burst failover? Cost ops: opening a quick cost ledger so Finance can flag any surprises.

lia: Noted for Finance. Dan — can you estimate worst-case spillover spend if we failover to eu-north1 for 30m?

dan: Quick back-of-envelope: ~0.6x of usual per-token (egress) plus inter-region egress at $0.02/GB. For 30m of peak traffic expect ~$800-$1.5k depending on traffic shape. I'll put a conservative cap and pre-approve up to $2k.

maria: Final ops checklist:
- [ ] Post tenant notice (lia)
- [ ] Run canary (sasha + ops)
- [ ] Observe telemetry for 10m (maria)
- [ ] Proceed cohorts if pass / abort & failover if fail
- [ ] Post-mortem if any regressions

kevin: LGTM. I'll reschedule high-cost batch jobs in scheduler to avoid collisions.

lia: Tenant notice drafted and sent to Product for sign-off.

maria: Cool. Will start a prep thread 30m before window with final node list and runbook links. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
